scope: All six supplied main pages, eight figures, Table 1, surface-charge equations and 47-entry bibliography. SI and cited full papers unreviewed.

bibliographic_scope.title: Photocatalytic Activity of PbS Quantum Dot/TiO2 Nanotube Composites
bibliographic_scope.authors: Chalita Ratanatawanate; Yuan Tao; Kenneth J. Balkus, Jr.

synthesis_routes.scope: Hydrothermal TNT preparation and workup; detailed prior method cited as reference 30.
TLA-linked PbS on both inside and outside TNT surfaces; prior method reference 29 cited.
DDAB blocking before TLA/lead/sulfide produces PbS inside TNTs; missing sulfide unit retained.

commercial_comparator.scope: Supplied P25; manufacturing recipe absent. No direct synthesis or training pair.

materials.purification: All chemicals used without further purification.

Table 1.scope: Literal dye properties and source structural drawings. Molecular masses are not used to infer or correct salt/hydrate identities.

protocol.lamp: Water-cooled Hanovia quartz mercury lamp inside dark box
protocol.environment: Room temperature, atmospheric condition; no invented numerical values
protocol.analysis: UV–vis supernatant at Table 1 maximum wavelength

visible_control.filter: Wavelengths <600 nm filtered; source compares irradiation >600 nm.

recycling.recovery: Recover catalyst, wash with DI water, introduce a fresh dye batch; no replenishment amount specified.
recycling.results: Both decline after first run. Authors report no significant PbS/TNT efficiency loss after the third run; TNT efficiency drops by 12% after 3 cycles, with percent-versus-percentage-point basis not defined. Exact bars are not digitized.
recycling.oxidation_check: FTIR showed no evidence of PbS oxidation; spectrum not shown.
recycling.appearance: Recovered PbS/TNTs unchanged in color; TNTs blue after 30 min due to remaining dye. Dried TNT catalyst bleaches after a few hours under room lighting, not a new preparation recipe.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–5, Photodegradation, Figures 2–8 and Recyclability

structure_scope.TNT: Open ends; inner 3–5 nm and outer 8–10 nm; BET 183 m2/g. Anatase assignment references prior work.
structure_scope.both_surface_PbS: About 4.3 nm TEM average over 100 counts; 5.6 nm XRD estimate (not shown). Do not conflate estimators or assign them to inside-only specimen.
structure_scope.inside_only_PbS: Figure 1d and text assign PbS inside pores. Same-size intention does not establish a separate measured size.
structure_scope.PbS_loading: Both types stated to contain 25 wt% PbS based on elemental analysis, reference 29.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–4, Characteristics and catalyst-comparison discussion

prior_and_model_context.scope: Authors quote prior work or interpret energetics; these values are not additional specimen-bound measurements in this main.

Galena_zeta_statement.note: Source calls this a zeta potential measurement, without unit. Do not silently convert it to pH or mV.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1, 2, 4–5, Introduction, characterization and Effect of PbS QDs

surface_charge_equations.scope: Qualitative acid–base surface interpretation, not a measured surface-species inventory

source_interpretation.topic: Thiolactic acid links PbS to the nanotube host
source_interpretation.text: The authors use thiolactic acid to attach PbS to TiO2 nanotubes. The both-surface route uses 0.6 M TLA; outer-surface DDAB blocking followed by 0.3 M TLA directs deposition into the pores. The lower TLA concentration was chosen in an effort to match size; a separate numerical inside-only size is not established.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Deposition and Figure 1 discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Charge and dye identity govern the assay comparison
source_interpretation.text: Around pH 6 the TNT surfaces favor cationic-dye adsorption. Figures 2–4 report the order PbS/TNTs > TNTs > PbS/TNTs (in) > P25 for methylene blue, methylene green and rhodamine B. For indigo carmine and rose bengal, Figures 5–6 instead show P25 > PbS/TNTs > PbS/TNTs (in) > TNTs. These are source activity comparisons, not additional syntheses.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Photocatalytic Activity and Figures 2–6

source_interpretation.text: The authors propose that PbS in the pores reduces accessible TNT surface and that remaining blocking reagent may also reduce activity. These are proposed explanations; remaining DDAB and pore-blocking fractions are not measured quantitatively in the main.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 4, Inside-only catalyst interpretation

source_interpretation.topic: Filtered-light response supports a qualified transfer mechanism
source_interpretation.text: With a Ray-sorb reactor filtering light below 600 nm, methylene-blue degradation is observed with PbS/TNTs whereas TNTs alone do not catalyze bleaching. Close contact through the linker is proposed to permit electron transfer. Literature energy levels and a size-dependent transfer limit are contextual estimates, not measured band alignment for a identified batch.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 4–5, Effect of PbS QDs and Figure 7

source_interpretation.topic: Recycling separates activity from catalyst recovery
source_interpretation.text: Figure 8 compares three methylene-blue runs at a 30 min readout. The authors discuss incomplete particle recovery, possible corrosion and dye adsorption as explanations for changes. FTIR is said to show no PbS oxidation, but the spectrum is not shown. No exact bar values are digitized.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 5, Recyclability and Figure 8

source_claims: Body text p. 2 says Figure 1c for P25.
Caption p. 3 assigns P25 a, TNTs b, PbS/TNTs c and inside-only d.
source_conflicts.handling: Caption mapping is used; conflicting body locator retained.

source_claims: Inside-only method p. 2 prints 0.5 Na2S solution with no unit.
Both-surface method separately specifies 0.5 M aqueous Na2S.
source_conflicts.handling: No unit is transferred between routes.
